q: In 1851, Heinrich Ruhmkorff showed how an electric spark could be produced by using a battery of only a few volts using an induction coil.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. The year 1851 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: An induction coil consists of a core of soft iron wires around which is wrapped a coil of a few turns of thick insulated wire called the primary.
e: True. That induction coil is built from a core of soft iron wires around which is wrapped a coil of a few turns of thick insulated wire called the primary. Coil of a few turns of thick insulated wire called the primary.

q: Around the primary of an induction coil is wound the secondary coil which has a few turns of thick insulated wire.
e: False. The right claim is this: Around the primary is wound the secondary coil which has many turns of thin insulated wire. Primary takes the AC supply; secondary delivers power to the load, with voltages in the turns ratio. The printed line wrongly says around the primary of an induction coil is wound the secondary coil which has a few turns of thick insulated wire.

q: The induction coil is used in the ignition system of motor cars.
e: True. This induction coil is used in the ignition system of motor cars. The induction coil is used in the ignition system of motor cars.

q: A generator is an electromagnetic device which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. A generator is an electromagnetic device which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

q: Most generators give out direct current and are called alternators.
e: False. The right claim is this: Most generators give out alternating current and are also called alternators. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. The printed line wrongly says most generators give out direct current and are called alternators.

q: AC generators work on the principle of Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
e: True. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. Faraday is the name attached to this result.

q: The induced current in an AC generator flows through the two slip rings and then through the external load.
e: True. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Flows through the two slip rings and then through the external load.

q: If the speed of rotating coil is doubled, both the frequency of the alternating current and the rate of cutting of the magnetic lines of force will be doubled.
e: True. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Rate of cutting of the magnetic lines of force will be doubled.

q: The induced electromotive force of a generator can be increased by increasing the speed of rotation of the coil.
e: True. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. Can be increased by increasing the speed of rotation of the coil.

q: The induced electromotive force of a generator can be increased by increasing the area and the number of turns in the coil.
e: True. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. By increasing the area and the number of turns in the coil.

q: There is a major structural difference between a generator and an electric motor.
e: False. The right claim is this: There is no structural difference between a generator and an electric motor. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. The printed line wrongly says there is a major structural difference between a generator and an electric motor.

q: In an electric motor, electrical energy is used to rotate the coil to provide mechanical energy.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. Electrical energy is used to rotate the coil to provide mechanical energy.

q: In the case of generators, mechanical energy is used to rotate the coil to produce electrical energy.
e: True. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. Mechanical energy is used to rotate the coil to produce electrical energy.

q: A transformer is used to change the frequency of an alternating current.
e: False. The right claim is this: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. The printed line wrongly says a transformer is used to change the frequency of an alternating current.

q: The core of a transformer is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance, called lamination.
e: True. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. Is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance, called lamination.

q: The coil connected to an alternating voltage source is called the primary coil.
e: True. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The coil connected to an alternating voltage source is called the primary coil.

q: The voltage in the secondary and the voltage in the primary of a transformer have different frequencies.
e: False. The right claim is this: The voltage in the secondary and the voltage in the primary have the same frequency. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The printed line wrongly says the voltage in the secondary and the voltage in the primary of a transformer have different frequencies.

q: The use of laminated iron (mumetal) core is to minimize the power loss due to the induced current flowing in the core.
e: True. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. The power loss due to the induced current flowing in the core.

q: As the product of voltage and current is the same on both coils of an ideal transformer, a transformer which increases the voltage will reduce the current in the same proportion.
e: True. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. Which increases the voltage will reduce the current in the same proportion.

q: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the transformer is called a step-down transformer.
e: False. The right claim is this: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is greater than the voltage applied to the primary, such a transformer is called a step-up transformer. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The printed line wrongly says if the secondary has more turns than the primary, the transformer is called a step-down transformer.

q: If the secondary has fewer turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is smaller than the voltage applied to the primary.
e: True. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. From the secondary is smaller than the voltage applied to the primary.

q: In a transformer, the changing magnetic field induces currents in the iron core itself which flow in little circles and are called eddy currents.
e: True. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. Core itself which flow in little circles and are called eddy currents.

q: The efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the input power to the output power.
e: False. The right claim is this: The efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the output power to the input power. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. The printed line wrongly says the efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the input power to the output power.

q: Most of the transformers have full load efficiency from 95% to 98.5%.
e: True. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. Most of the transformers have full load efficiency from 95% to 98.5%.

q: Soft magnetic material should be used to make the core to improve the efficiency of a transformer.
e: True. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio. Used to make the core to improve the efficiency of a transformer.

q: High-resistance copper wires should be used as coils to reduce energy loss in the form of heat in a transformer.
e: False. The right claim is this: Low-resistance copper wires should be used as coils to reduce energy loss in the form of heat. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. The printed line wrongly says high-resistance copper wires should be used as coils to reduce energy loss in the form of heat in a transformer.

q: Transformers work on AC, but not on DC.
e: True. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery. Transformers work on AC, but not on DC.

q: A transformer connected to a DC supply can be damaged as the high current flowed through the input coil can make it overheat.
e: True. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery. The high current flowed through the input coil can make it overheat.
